summary: 1935 CCC steel tower and cabin on Toxaway Mountain, NC; a 2016 blog copy of a library column calls it manned; a 2018 surplus notice said the lease ended and removal was needed.

facts.design: Steel tower, 45 ft 9 in, with a one-room cabin
facts.status_note: Lease on the tower site was terminated and the structure needed removal after a 2018 state surplus auction notice; no source confirms it still stands

staffing.status: reported manned in a library column

facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

events.note: Built by CCC Company 3448 from Camp Sledge, Brevard: 45 ft 9 in steel tower with one-room cabin, cost $880.19
Surplus state property auction opened March 22, 2018; lease for the tower site terminated; structure needed to be removed (per Forest Lookouts). No source confirms removal.

corrections.why: Both sources give the tower as 45 ft 9 in (45-foot 9-inch). That is 13.94 m, which rounds to 13.9 m, not 13.7 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A library column, copied to a blog in October 2016, calls the tower one of two still-manned lookouts in western NC. A 2018 surplus notice says the lease ended and the structure needed removal. The manned claim predates the notice, and no source shows the tower's condition after 2018.

sources.title: Lookout Towers Played Role in Preserving Forests
The Rowell Bosse North Carolina Room: Lookout Towers

notes_for_editor: Current status is unknown. No source says whether the tower still stands or whether the site is public, so no access or visit facts are recorded. The brief's height of 13.7 m is corrected to 13.9 m from the 45 ft 9 in figure. The 'still manned' statement comes from a library column with no date in its text; the 2016 date is confirmed by the blog's own date line (Monday, October 24, 2016), which is why as_of is 2016-10. The surplus auction notice (ncstatesurplus.com, cited on Forest Lookouts) was not fetched directly; a fetch of that listing would confirm the 2018 sale and whether the tower was removed. A SummitPost page makes the same undated 'one of two manned' claim and was not cited.
